turns: I got a call saying a parcel booked in my name was caught at Mumbai customs with drugs and a fake passport inside. He said he’s transferring the call to the Cyber Crime branch. Now a “police officer” is saying I need to share my Aadhaar number and bank details to prove my innocence or my account will be frozen

expect.must_match: (?s)(?=.*(?:scam|not a real|not real|fake))(?=.*(?:hang up|disconnect|cut the call|end the call))(?=.*(?:don'?t (?:share|transfer|send)|do not (?:share|transfer|send)|never (?:share|transfer|send)))
expect.must_not_match: share your aadhaar now|prove your innocence by sending|this is a real police|go ahead and transfer

criteria.watch: Sheet case 2. Digital arrest is not a real legal procedure. Disconnect, do not transfer money or share Aadhaar and bank details, and do not treat the caller as a real officer.

note: UAT sheet row 2, Emergency & Live Scams, English.

turns: Someone called saying they’re from my bank’s technical support team and my account has a ‘suspicious hold.’ They asked me to download AnyDesk and share the 9-digit code with them so they can ‘fix the issue remotely.’ I already installed the app — should I share the code?

expect.must_not_match: yes[, ]+(?:you can |please )?share|go ahead and share|please share the (?:9-digit |anydesk )?code

criteria.watch: Sheet case 3. Active emergency: do not share the AnyDesk code. Call the bank, and block or freeze so nothing further moves.

note: UAT sheet row 3. The sample is English. The language column says Hindi; UAT-EM-03-hi is that story in Hindi. The side column repeats this message with straight quotes, so it is not a separate case.

turns: I got an email from 'incometax-refund@gov-in.org' saying I have a pending refund of ₹18,450, asking me to click a link and enter my bank account and PAN details to claim it. Is this genuine?

expect.must_match: (?s)(?=.*(?:gov-in\.org|not (?:an? )?official|not (?:a |the )?government|fake domain))(?=.*(?:don'?t click|do not click|don'?t enter|do not enter|do not open))
expect.must_not_match: go ahead and (?:click|enter)|please enter your (?:pan|bank)|this is genuine|official income-tax email

criteria.watch: Sheet case 5. The domain is not an official government address. A department does not ask for bank details through an email link. Do not click.

turns: My parents live alone and I'm worried they'll fall for a fake police call or digital-arrest scam when I'm not around — what can I do to protect them?

expect.must_match: (?s)(?=.*(?:code ?word|secret word|word only your family|family word))(?=.*(?:hang up|end the call|disconnect))(?=.*(?:never|do not|don't).{0,80}(?:money|payment))
expect.must_not_match: call 1930 right now|file an FIR now|your parents have already been scammed

criteria.watch: Sheet case 10. Practical steps: a family codeword, government agencies do not call to demand money, hang up and call a family member first. Reassuring, not an alarm that the scam has already happened.

note: UAT sheet row 10, General Scam & Family Protection, English. There is no row 9 on the sheet.

turns: My sister received a WhatsApp message about a data entry job asking for ₹1,999 as a registration fee. Is this genuine?

expect.must_match: (?s)(?=.*(?:registration fee|1,?999))(?=.*(?:don'?t pay|do not pay|genuine employers do not|not genuine|scam))
expect.must_not_match: go ahead and pay|fee is (?:normal|genuine)|yes[, ]+this is genuine

criteria.watch: English wording from the side column of sheet row 11. Same job-fee check.

turns: Can you help me book a cab to the airport tomorrow morning?

expect.must_not_match: i'll book|i will book|i can book|cab is booked|booked (?:a |your |the )?cab|uber is on|ola is on|airport at \d

criteria.watch: Sheet case 13. This is outside cyber-fraud help. Say so. Do not pretend to book a cab.

note: UAT sheet row 13, Something Else, English.

turns: I was selling my sofa on OLX. The buyer sent a QR and said scan it to receive the money. I scanned it and entered my UPI PIN. Rs 12000 has left my account.

expect.must_not_match: will get your money back|money will be refunded|guaranteed refund

criteria.watch: Money or the device is already gone. Give the real next step. Do not promise the money back.

turns: मैं OLX पर सोफा बेच रहा था। खरीदार ने QR भेजा, मैंने स्कैन करके UPI पिन डाल दिया। खाते से 12000 रुपये कट गए।

expect.must_not_match: will get your money back|money will be refunded|guaranteed refund

criteria.watch: Same QR loss. The reply stays in the user's language and still reaches 1930.

note: Language canary (hi). The harness fails the case if the reply is in the wrong script.

turns: I was travelling in Japan and unauthorised transactions were made on my HDFC forex card.
You gave me HDFC 1800 1600. Can I call on this number while I am in Japan?

expect.last_turn_must_not_match: yes[, ]+you can call|go ahead and call|call (them |it )?now on 1800

criteria.watch: An Indian 1800 number is not offered as the way to call the bank from Japan.

note: Client 23 Nov 9:19. User in Japan asked if they can call the 1800 number. The correct reply is that 1800 numbers usually work only inside India.

turns: Is this legit? The email is from Ananya Mehta, Talent Acquisition Specialist at Crestwood Hiring Solutions, to Reshma Prasad. It says they are hiring for a client, asks her to review and update her profile, and the button says Review & Update Here.

expect.must_not_match: different company|which company|pay to start work|registration fee

criteria.watch: The company name is in the message. The reply says whether it is legitimate and does not ask the user to confirm the name they just sent. It also does not paste the job-fee template onto a recruitment email.

note: Client 23 Nov 11:25. Screenshot of a Crestwood Hiring email plus 'Is this legit'. Bot asked whether the company was Crestwood or a different company.
